MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 27: Royce Lewis #23 of the Minnesota Twins celebrates his solo home run as he rounds the bases against the Texas Rangers in the eighth inning at Target Field on September 27, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Twins defeated the Rangers 6-4. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty
 Friday, November 20, marks an important day on the Major League Baseball calendar, as it's the 'non-tender' deadline for arbitration-level players.
 One name to watch, according to many MLB insiders, is Minnesota Twins infielder Royce Lewis.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jon Morosi wrote (via X.com):
 "Royce Lewis is a name to follow today. He is eligible for salary arbitration, and the Twins are considering 3 options: tender, non-tender, and trade."
 If the Twins decide to trade Lewis, the Atlanta Braves stand out as a top option and a team to certainly keep an eye on.
 More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Signing of Intriguing 24-Year-Old Pitcher 
 Should the Braves Trade for Royce Lewis?
 GettyMINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – SEPTEMBER 27: Royce Lewis #23 of the Minnesota Twins celebrates his solo home run as he rounds the bases against the Texas Rangers in the eighth inning at Target Field on September 27, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Twins defeated the Rangers 6-4. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images)
 Royce Lewis, a five-year MLB veteran and former No. 1 overall draft pick by the Twins in 2017, has experience around the infield, and considering he came up as a shortstop, he could fill-in that big hole for the Braves.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yes, Atlanta's front office (Alex Anthopoulos) should consider trading for Royce Lewis.
Anthopoulos recently noted that he is exploring the shortstop market, and Lewis stands out as a perfect low-cost option with immense upside.
 Injuries have certainly been part of Lewis's MLB story, but in 2026, he played in 125 games and hit 15 home runs, while driving in over 55 runs across 450+ at-bats.
